svg.title: How workers share one checkout
svg.desc: Animated diagram. Three workers, docs-T1, docs-T2 and docs-T3, edit only their own files in one folder, ~/projects/site, on one branch. mike's watcher reads the folder once a second and records each changed file and the session that changed it. fleet_commit takes only a task's files into a private index, adds a Fleet-Seat line, commits and pushes. Checks run in clean copies of a commit under .claude/worktrees/ (mike-check, mike-check-2 and mike-gate), so unfinished edits in the folder never reach them.
svg.text: One folder, one branch, clean copies for checks

g.text: a clean copy of one commit;
One folder, one branch, no copies
Every worker edits the same checkout. T1 changes only install.md,
T2 only quickstart.md. Neither touches the other's file.
Once a second mike reads the folder and records each changed file
and the session that changed it.
fleet_commit takes only the task's files
It builds the commit in a private index from install.md alone,
adds a Fleet-Seat line naming the session, commits and pushes.
The check runs in a clean copy
quickstart.md is not in that copy, so it cannot spoil the result.
The gate runs on the pushed commit
The gate command has its own clean copy, mike-gate.
Two checks can run at once
T2 commits quickstart.md the same way, and its check takes
the second slot, mike-check-2, while the first is still busy.
When T1 and T2 have passed, T3's worker edits scripts/check-links
in the same checkout and sees their commits at once.
